title: Ecosystem profiles
description: A build system's ecosystem described as data (HITLD-886): its manifests, lockfiles, version sources, the folders walks skip and its shareable caches. A profile never holds a command: this is not an owner configuration schema, so no property here may be run, and a code-running key is refused wherever it appears. The commands for a project's paths live only in policy.json ecosystems.use. The built-in profiles shipped with hitld (core/lib/ecosystems/profiles.json) are a file of this shape; a project's own profiles in policy.json ecosystems.profiles use its profile definition.

profiles.description: The built-in profiles, one per ecosystem.

fileName.description: A file or folder name, matched in any folder: no path separator.

name.description: The profile's name, which ecosystems.use names.

extends.description: A project's own profile only: the built-in profile it starts from. Each list given here replaces the built-in's list; a list left out is the built-in's.

manifests.description: The file names that declare dependencies, such as package.json or Cargo.toml.

lockfiles.description: The file names that pin resolved dependencies, such as package-lock.json or Cargo.lock.

version_sources.description: Where a package's version is read: a file, its format and the key path to the version. Read by release in a later slice; until then, release.packages version_source is what release reads.

file.description: A repository path: relative to the repository root, with no `..` segment, not starting with `~`, and a file rather than a glob. `hitld work check` refuses one that is not.

key.description: The key path to the version, dot-separated, such as version or package.version.

skip_folders.description: Folder names walks skip, wherever they are: installed dependencies and build output, such as node_modules or target. A name, never a path: `hitld work check` refuses one with a separator or `..`.

caches.description: Dependency caches the ecosystem's own tool can share between worktrees, each named by the environment variable that points the tool at it. Nothing reads this yet: in this release hitld only validates it, and sets, exports or creates nothing from it (a later slice, HITLD-925, has setup and checks export the variable, pointing at the tool's default folder or a machine-file path, and the disk report show the folder's size). hitld never creates links itself.

variable.description: The environment variable that sets the cache's folder, and nothing else. An allowlist, compared without regard to case: a known cache variable (npm_config_cache, npm_config_store_dir, PNPM_STORE_DIR, YARN_CACHE_FOLDER, GOCACHE, GOMODCACHE, PIP_CACHE_DIR, UV_CACHE_DIR, POETRY_CACHE_DIR, BUNDLE_USER_CACHE, COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR, XDG_CACHE_HOME, PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX, PRE_COMMIT_HOME, HF_HOME), or a name ending in _CACHE, _CACHE_DIR, _CACHE_FOLDER or _STORE_DIR that the dynamic loader or git does not read (LD_*, DYLD_*, GIT_*) and that is not a switch (_ENABLE_, _DISABLE_, _USE_, _NO_, _SKIP_). `hitld work check` refuses any other, since a variable that names a home folder, configuration, credentials, a search path or flags (CARGO_HOME and GRADLE_USER_HOME hold configuration and init scripts) can change what a tool runs.
